title: Une belle robe rouge
en: Where adjectives go: before or after the noun
intro: In English, adjectives always come before the noun. In French, most come **after** it (*une robe rouge*) — but a small group of very common ones come **before** (*une belle robe*). Remember them with **BAGS**: Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size.

cases.label: most adjectives: after the noun
cases.rule: Colours, nationalities, shapes and most other adjectives go **after** the noun: *une robe rouge, un film français, un repas délicieux*.

cases.label: BAGS: before the noun
cases.rule: **B**eauty (beau, joli), **A**ge (jeune, vieux, nouveau), **G**oodness (bon, mauvais), **S**ize (grand, petit, gros) go **before**: *une belle robe, un petit chapeau*.

cases.label: bel, nouvel, vieil
cases.rule: Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel or silent h: **beau → bel, nouveau → nouvel, vieux → vieil**: *un bel appartement, un nouvel ami, un vieil homme*.

cases.label: two adjectives
cases.rule: Each one goes in its usual place: *une belle robe rouge*. Two adjectives after the noun are joined with **et**: *un t-shirt blanc et bleu*.

cases.label: de belles robes (des → de)
cases.rule: In careful French, **des** becomes **de** when an adjective comes before a plural noun: *de belles robes, de grands yeux*. In speech you'll also hear *des*.

cases.label: before or after: a different meaning
cases.rule: A few adjectives change meaning: *un grand homme* (great) / *un homme grand* (tall); *mon ancien professeur* (former) / *un meuble ancien* (antique); *un cher ami* (dear) / *une robe chère* (expensive).

sections.title: 1. Most adjectives go after the noun
text: Colours, nationalities, shapes and longer adjectives come **after** the noun — the opposite of English.

sections.title: 2. BAGS: a few short adjectives go before

head: Group
Examples
rows: une belle robe · un joli sac
un jeune homme · un vieux pull · une nouvelle veste
un bon repas · un mauvais film
un grand manteau · un petit chapeau · un gros chien

sections.title: 3. bel, nouvel, vieil
text: Three BAGS adjectives have a special form before a masculine noun that starts with a vowel or a silent h — it makes the words flow together.
sections.tip: **bel, nouvel, vieil** sound exactly like the feminine **belle, nouvelle, vieille**.

sections.title: 5. des → de before an adjective
text: In careful French, when an adjective comes **before** a plural noun, **des** becomes **de**. In everyday speech you'll often hear *des* anyway.
sections.tip: With the adjective after the noun, keep **des**: *des robes rouges*.

story.title: Le nouveau look de Hugo
story.en: Hugo has a job interview — and needs new clothes.

lines.fr: Hugo a un entretien pour un travail lundi. Il n'a pas de vêtements élégants…
lines.en: Hugo has a job interview on Monday. He has no smart clothes…

lines.fr: J'ai seulement {un vieux jean|pla-bags} et {des t-shirts noirs|pla-after}.
lines.en: I only have old jeans and black T-shirts.

lines.fr: On va au magasin ! Tu as besoin d'{une belle chemise blanche|pla-two}.
lines.en: Let's go to the shop! You need a nice white shirt.

lines.fr: Et d'{un pantalon élégant|pla-after}, et d'{une veste noire|pla-after}.
lines.en: And smart trousers, and a black jacket.

lines.fr: Au magasin, Hugo essaie un costume.
lines.en: At the shop, Hugo tries on a suit.

lines.fr: Oh, Hugo ! Tu es {un bel homme|pla-bel} !
lines.en: Oh, Hugo! You're a handsome man!

lines.fr: Avec ces vêtements, tu as l'air d'{un homme important|pla-after}.
lines.en: In these clothes, you look like an important man.
And the shoes? I've got old trainers…

lines.fr: Non ! Il faut {de belles chaussures noires|pla-two}.
lines.en: No! You need nice black shoes.

lines.fr: Ce costume est parfait. C'est {un bon choix|pla-bags}, monsieur.
lines.en: This suit is perfect. It's a good choice, sir.
Thank you. How much is it?

lines.fr: Trois cents euros ?! C'est {un costume cher|pla-meaning} !
lines.en: Three hundred euros?! That's an expensive suit!

lines.fr: C'est pour ton entretien, Hugo. Et c'est le cadeau de {ta chère sœur|pla-meaning} !
lines.en: It's for your interview, Hugo. And it's a present from your dear sister!

lines.fr: Merci, Léa ! Tu es {une sœur formidable|pla-after}.
lines.en: Thank you, Léa! You're a wonderful sister.

quiz.q: How do you say “a red dress”?
How do you say “a French film”?
How do you say “a beautiful dress”?
How do you say “a small hat”?
Which adjectives usually go BEFORE the noun?
How do you say “a beautiful red dress”?
How do you say “a white and blue T-shirt”?

quiz.why: Adjective before a plural noun: careful French uses **de**.
